storage.format: JSON per file: one pretty-printed JSON document per session (JSON.stringify(session, undefined, 2)), 2-space indent, whole document = {sessionId,title,workspaceDirectory,history[],mode?,chatModelTitle?,usage?}. NOT JSONL, NOT one record per line. Plus a JSON index file sessions.json. history[] entries are ChatHistoryItem {message,contextItems,toolCallStates?,promptLogs?,reasoning?}.
storage.append_semantics: WHOLE-FILE REWRITE, not append-only. core/util/history.ts HistoryManager.save() -> fs.writeFileSync(sessionPath, JSON.stringify(orderedSession, undefined, 2)) on every change, and also rewrites sessions.json. CLI (extensions/cli/src/services/ChatHistoryService.ts setHistoryInternal -> updateSessionHistory -> saveSession) rewrites on EVERY history mutation (user msg, assistant msg with tool calls, each tool status change 'calling'->'done', tool result) => effectively live during the agent loop. VS Code/JetBrains call core 'history/save' from saveCurrentSession, dispatched in gui/src/redux/thunks/streamThunkWrapper.tsx AFTER each completed stream => written once per finished turn, not per tool call. Consequence: the existing append-only LogTailer cannot be used; a snapshot+diff adapter is required.
storage.session_file_naming: <sessionId>.json where sessionId is a uuid-v4 (uuidv4() in both gui/src/redux/slices/sessionSlice.ts and extensions/cli/src/session.ts). The sibling index file 'sessions.json' must be excluded by is_session_log. Session ids are NOT grouped by project; grouping is by the workspaceDirectory field inside each file (historyManager.list({workspaceDirectory}) filters on it).

fields.project: RECOVERABLE. Session.workspaceDirectory (absolute path) -> publish only its basename. CLI sets it to process.cwd(); VS Code GUI sets window.workspacePaths?.[0] || "". Per core/util/paths.ts the store is global (~/.continue/sessions), so project identity comes from the field, not the directory.
fields.model: RECOVERABLE. Session.chatModelTitle (e.g. 'Claude 3.5 Sonnet') and per-item promptLogs[].modelTitle / promptLogs[].modelProvider (core/index.d.ts PromptLog). These are user-configured titles, not raw model ids - sanitize like events.rs deepseek_model_label (allow [A-Za-z0-9-_.:/@], <=128 chars, else drop).
fields.file_basename: RECOVERABLE from tool arguments only. Args holding paths: filepath (read_file, read_file_range, edit_existing_file, single_find_and_replace, multi_edit, create_new_file), dirPath (ls), directory_path (view_subdirectory), plus MCP tools' own 'path'/'file_path'. Extract basename only, never the full path. core/tools/builtIn.ts BuiltInToolNames = read_file, read_file_range, edit_existing_file, single_find_and_replace, multi_edit, read_currently_open_file, create_new_file, run_terminal_command, grep_search, file_glob_search, search_web, view_diff, ls, create_rule_block, request_rule, fetch_url_content, codebase, read_skill, view_repo_map, view_subdirectory.
fields.tool_activity: RECOVERABLE. toolCallStates[].toolCall.function.name + .arguments (JSON string) + .parsedArgs; status in generating|generated|calling|errored|done|canceled; output[].content holds the raw result (must never be published). Tool results also appear as message.role=='tool' with toolCallId. Normalize with existing events.rs classify_tool()/extract_file_basename()/language_from_file().
fields.phase: PARTIALLY RECOVERABLE. Session.mode = 'chat'|'agent'|'plan'|'background' (MessageModes, GUI default 'agent'); running vs waiting derives from toolCallStates[].status ('calling' => Running tools; 'generated' => awaiting approval; assistant message with reasoning.active => Thinking). Turn boundary = user message; completion = assistant message with no toolCalls.
fields.timestamps: NOT RECOVERABLE per event. ChatHistoryItem has no timestamp field and createHistoryItem (core/util/messageConversion.ts) adds none. Only: reasoning.startAt/endAt (ms, rare), sessions.json dateCreated = String(Date.now()) at session creation, and file mtime. The Discodex elapsed timer must fall back to 'first time Discodex observed this turn' or the session file mtime, so it is approximate, not a true turn timer.

parser_strategy: Not line-based. Read the whole session file (bounded, e.g. <=32 MB), serde_json::from_str into a ContinueSession view {sessionId,title,workspaceDirectory,history[],mode,chatModelTitle}, and DIFF it against a per-file cursor that stores (a) how many history items were already consumed and (b) the last known ToolStatus per toolCallId. Emit events only for the delta: new history items and status transitions. Mapping: SessionMetadata{project: basename(workspaceDirectory), cwd} + AgentDetected{sanitized chatModelTitle} on first sight; item.message.role=='user' -> TaskStarted; item.message.role=='thinking' or item.reasoning.active -> Thinking{reasoning: None} (never ship reasoning text); assistant item -> for each toolCallState: status 'calling'/'generated' -> TrackedToolStarted{call_id, activity{label: classify_tool(name), file: basename(filepath|dirPath|path), language: language_from_file(basename)}}, status 'done'|'errored'|'canceled' -> TrackedToolFinished{call_id}; assistant message with no toolCalls -> TerminalCandidate (not Completed, so the 4s debounce in state.rs shows the project/file briefly instead of vanishing). Implementation shape that preserves the existing contract: emit these as synthetic single-line JSON records and feed them through the existing parse_line_for(Provider::Continue, line) path, so main.rs's apply_lines() stays unchanged.

   - Privacy is preserved by construction: only basename / fixed labels / model id / phase / start time cross the boundary; the file itself (which contains prompts) never leaves the process.

risks: Storage is a REWRITTEN JSON snapshot, not an append-only stream: the existing LogTailer (offset + newline splitting) cannot parse it and would mis-read it. Requires a new snapshot+diff path in watcher.rs/main.rs - the single biggest change vs the Codex/Antigravity adapters.

VS Code / JetBrains only write the session file at the END of a turn (saveCurrentSession after the stream resolves), so there is no live 'current file' during the agent run; presence can only flash per turn. Only the Continue CLI (cn) rewrites live (on every tool status change).

No per-event timestamps exist in the file (ChatHistoryItem has no timestamp; createHistoryItem adds none), so the elapsed timer is approximate - it can only start when Discodex first observes the turn. This is a real fidelity gap vs Codex/DSH/Claude Code.

The session file contains the full conversation (prompts, assistant text, tool args, tool output). A parser bug could leak content; every extraction must be allowlist-based (fixed labels, basename, sanitized model id) and the 'title' field (derived from the user's prompt) must never be published.
sessions.json is a sibling index in the same folder and looks like a session file; the filename rule must explicitly exclude it or Discodex will parse the index as a session.

Schema churn: Session/ChatHistoryItem/ToolStatus live in core/index.d.ts and change often; tool arg names (filepath vs path vs dirPath) and the store location (CONTINUE_GLOBAL_DIR) can change. Degradation must be to 'no session data' (fall back to focused detection), never to garbage presence.

Global (not per-workspace) store means many unrelated projects' sessions sit in one folder; Discodex must pick the active session (newest mtime) and the workspace comes from the workspaceDirectory field, not the path - a session from another project could otherwise win the presence.

has_session_tracking() semantics: adding Continue to that list permanently disables the focused-window fallback for Continue (main.rs:66,112), which would regress the common 'Continue open in VS Code but no active chat' case unless a separate 'prefers session data' flag is introduced.

No lobehub icon exists for Continue (all continue*.png probes 404), so the provider must use an upstream raw.githubusercontent.com logo URL instead of the pinned jsDelivr convention - a different supply chain from the other providers.

summary: Continue.dev DOES store sessions locally in a machine-readable form, so it is viable, but not with the existing tailer: the store is one pretty-printed JSON document per session at %USERPROFILE%\.continue\sessions\<uuid-v4>.json (global per-user, not per-workspace), rewritten in full (fs.writeFileSync) rather than appended. The CLI (@continuedev/cli, bin cn) rewrites on every history mutation (each tool status change) so it is effectively live; the VS Code extension and JetBrains plugin call core 'history/save' once per completed turn, so they only update at turn end. Recoverable without shipping conversation text: project (basename of workspaceDirectory), model (chatModelTitle), tool name + args (toolCallStates[].toolCall.function.name/.arguments -> filepath/dirPath), tool status (generating|generated|calling|errored|done|canceled), turn boundaries (user messages), completion (assistant message with no tool calls), and session mode (chat|agent|plan|background). NOT recoverable: per-event timestamps (ChatHistoryItem has none), so the elapsed timer is only approximate. Everything needed lives in plain JSON - no state.vscdb, no SQLite crate, no encryption, no auth token required. Verdict partial: field coverage is Codex/DSH-level for the CLI path, but delivery is a rewritten snapshot (needs a snapshot+diff adapter) and the timer is approximate; the IDE path only updates at turn end.
